identity_evidence: The cartridge names this class daSanbo_c, NOT Pokey. extracted/overlays/overlay_0096.bin file offset 0x2280 holds the bytes '9daSanbo_c�' -- the strict length-prefixed _ZTS form, prefix 9 == len("daSanbo_c"). Module base 0x02135700 puts that string at 0x02137980, which config/arm9/overlays/ov096/symbols.txt names _ZTS9daSanbo_c. It is bound to THIS class and not to a neighbour, by a two-hop read straight out of the image: the vtable at 0x021379d8 has its RTTI header word at 0x021379d4, which holds 0x0213798c; the __si_class_type_info record at 0x0213798c holds {+0 0x0209a764 = arm9 _ZTVN3abi20__si_class_type_infoE, +4 0x02137980 -> '9daSanbo_c', +8 0x0208e390 = _ZTI8dActor_c}. So the vtable that symbols.txt spells _ZTV5Pokey points at the typeinfo whose name string is daSanbo_c. 'Pokey' is the coined English name for the same enemy; Sanbo is its Japanese name (romaji), which the cartridge also uses for its assets (data/enemy/sanbo/sanbo_head.bmd, sanbo_body.bmd in overlay_0000.bin) and for the SANBO / SANBO_BODY profile labels in arm9_dec.bin.

tu_structure.tu_map_disagreement:
build/tu_map.json (regenerated at this revision with build/rtti_vtables.json present, so NOT the degraded run -- it reports 691 TUs / 333 with a class, the correct signature, not 692/332) segments ov096 into FOUR units, and two of them are wrong:
  unit 0 0x02135700..0x02136d10 classes=[Pokey]   34 functions
  unit 1 0x02136d10..0x02136db0 classes=[]         2 functions (daSanbo_c_classInit_SANBO_BODY, daSanbo_c_classInit_SANBO)
  unit 2 0x02136db0..0x021376bc classes=[Tornado] 10 functions
  unit 3 0x021376bc..0x0213770c classes=[]         1 function  (daTor_c_classInit)
Units 1 and 3 are artifacts: tu_map does not recognise '_classInit' as a factory spelling, so it cuts a boundary in front of every factory and leaves the resulting unit class-less. The cartridge disagrees on two independent counts -- the factories store this class vptr (0x021379d8) and inline this class constructor, and there are only 2 static initializers and 2 .ctor entries for what tu_map calls 4 TUs. The real segmentation is 2 TUs: units 0+1 are daSanbo_c, units 2+3 are daTor_c.
This is also the origin of the queue row shard_count 34: it inherits tu_map unit 0 and therefore omits the two factory shards.

blockers_for_the_writer: THE VTABLE MUST NOT BE EMITTED BY THE PROMOTED TU. .data is unowned (see data_ownership), so _ZTV, _ZTI and _ZTS are carried from the cartridge. If the TU emits its own, the RTTI name string alone breaks the band: this class must be spelled `Pokey` in source (all 36 shards, all symbols.txt rows and the existing header already use _ZN5Pokey...), so mwccarm would emit _ZTS5Pokey = '5Pokey\0' (7 bytes) where the ROM has '9daSanbo_c\0' (11 bytes) -- a 4-byte shift that moves _ZTI, both profiles and both vtables. Because the TU emits no RTTI, the coined spelling costs nothing; but only while it emits none.

DO NOT DEFINE THE STATE TABLE IN THE TU. The 12 PMF records live in unowned .data and are written at runtime by __sinit_ov096_0213770c, which is its own delinked shard (src/__sinit_ov096_0213770c.c). A file-scope PMF array with a dynamic initializer in the promoted .cpp would make mwccarm generate a second __sinit and duplicate that shard.

RENAMING ANY OF THE 12 PMF TARGETS IS A TWO-FILE EDIT. dsd resolves those .data records by symbol NAME; a renamed member whose new mangled name is not in ov096/symbols.txt in the same commit links as 0x00000000, and no stage-2 or stage-3 byte gate sees it.

STAGE 3B CEILING IS NAME RECOVERY, NOT CODEGEN. 10 of the 36 members already carry mangled _ZN5Pokey names and convert as a pure codegen question. The other 26 (12 PMF handlers, 12 helpers, 2 factories) carry auto-generated names -- func_ov096_* and daSanbo_c_classInit_* -- so converting them means renaming, with the symbols.txt edit above. State that wall in the result rather than reporting a bare fraction.

extern "C" REGION PLACEMENT. Any member kept as a free function must stay inside the one file-scope extern "C" region, and that region must sit after the last surviving func_* member, because a class member function cannot live inside it.

The PMF record's second word is 0 in all 12 records, so I cannot tell whether it is a this-adjustment or a virtual-index field. Only the 8-byte {fn,0} shape is proven.
The signature of the pointed-to members is NOT proven -- nothing in the record fixes the return type or parameter list of `void (Pokey::*)()`.

The g_profile_* record is 7 words (0x1c) and only two fields are proven: word0 is the classInit function pointer, and the LOW halfword of word1 is the ACTOR_SPAWN_TABLE index (0xf0 / 0xf1). The high halfword (0x005f / 0x0060) and words 2..6 (0x10000002, 0x001f4000, 0x001f4000, 0x01000000, 0x01000000) are unidentified. There is no ActorProfile struct in include/ at this base.

SOURCE ORDER within the TU is NOT proven. mwccarm emits .text in reverse source order, which would put daSanbo_c_classInit_SANBO (0x02136d60) first and _ZN5PokeyD1Ev (0x02135700) last, but that convention is explicitly unreliable to verify against generated src/ files and I did not verify it here. Emission order is a hard gate at link time -- treat it as the writer's measurement, not my fact.

The Matrix4x3 TYPE at 0x33c is corroboration from include/Pokey.h. What the ROM proves is the 0x30-byte extent (`add ip,r4,#0x33c`, stores at 0x360/0x364/0x368, next proven field at 0x36c) -- not that it is a matrix.

Whether daSanbo_c's TU byte-matches at all is unmeasured. I ran no compile, no tubuild.py verify, no linkcheck and no rombuild. `promotion_route: text-only` is the queue's estimate, re-read at this base, not a result of mine.
The coined-name search covered 8-bit ASCII only. A UTF-16 or otherwise wide-encoded 'Pokey' would not have been found.
